response.markdown_report:
### Insights and directions

**Starting-point insights.** (1) SASRec’s causal encoder permits inexpensive objective ablations; sampled margins do not establish HR@10. (2) Electronics’ 14.95% wrong rankings and −0.4812 lower-decile margin motivate stronger discrimination. Similar embedding-alignment scores do not establish collapse as the cause. (3) Users report stale-interest interference and broadly plausible recommendations. Recent conditioning addresses these hypotheses; compatibility and satisfied demand remain unobserved.

**Related-work insights.** (1) gSASRec corrects sampling-induced overconfidence; additional negatives alone are different [1]. (2) Scalable Cross-Entropy motivates informative competitors [2]. (3) Long/short-term modeling supports recent-intent conditioning [3], without establishing this exact fusion. ReZero supports identity-preserving initialization [5].

### Framework and candidate ideas

| Direction | Minimal intervention | Intended diagnostic target |
|---|---|---|
| Objective | Multi-negative candidate cross-entropy | Weak positive–negative separation |
| Intent | Recent-window residual gate | Historical-interest interference |
| Behavioral association | Smoothed directed transitions | Broad similarity without directional support |

Scores use 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each assessment includes a strength and limitation.

1. **Multi-negative candidate cross-entropy** [1,2]. Originality **3**: useful adaptation / established objective; potential **7**: scalable baseline / sampler-sensitive; user alignment **5**: distinguishes competitors / lacks explicit intent; model alignment **9**: targets separation / sampled gains may not transfer; difficulty **4**: compact loss / prefix masking requires care.
2. **Recent-conditioned SASRec with multi-negative training** [2,3,5]. Originality **4**: focused combination / familiar components; potential **7**: reusable mechanism / uncertain gains; user alignment **8**: targets stale interests and broad matches / cannot establish compatibility; model alignment **9**: targets weak separation / unobserved negatives may be relevant; difficulty **6**: compact architecture / sampling, diagnostics and predictor synchronization add work.
3. **SASRec plus directed transition residual**. Originality **4**: directional evidence / established hybrid; potential **6**: inexpensive / sparse transitions; user alignment **6**: recent associations / order does not prove usefulness; model alignment **6**: additional ranking evidence / popularity shortcuts; difficulty **4**: simple counts / smoothing requires validation.

### Selected idea

Select **idea 2** at 0% progress, contingent on ablations. It targets stale-history interference and broad associations displacing current matches, plus Electronics’ weak sampled separation. These are hypotheses, not demonstrated improvements.

Use a five-item causal exponential mean, decay **0.7**, including the current input item, with padding excluded. Fuse as **z=h+αg(h,r)P(r)**, with **α=0**, identity-initialized projection and gate bias **−1**; omit outer LayerNorm to preserve baseline features initially. Train against **32 uniform negatives**, excluding target and observed prefix, retaining replacement duplicates. Call this candidate discrimination, not full-catalog softmax.

Preregister baseline, objective-only, fusion-only and combined variants; hold routing, splits, seeds **0/42/42**, checkpoint opportunities and selection rules fixed. Preserve the **200-epoch environment default**. Profile GPU cost, reserve contingency, and compare complete four-category configurations within **43,200 aggregate GPU-seconds**. Select only by pinned macro validation HR@10; report category results. Fixed candidates limit generalization [6]; repeated selection risks optimism [7]. Paired user bootstrap intervals are descriptive after selection.

Update predictor generation and diagnostic scoring together. Track measured margins, retain all diagnostic interfaces, and mark unavailable metadata attribution explicitly. Keep the simpler baseline when evidence is inconclusive.

idea.description: Recent-conditioned SASRec with multi-negative candidate cross-entropy: add an initially inactive, gated recent-history correction to causal SASRec features and train against 32 uniformly sampled alternatives. Compare it with baseline, objective-only and fusion-only variants.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies stale historical interests and broadly plausible associations displacing specific current matches. Recent conditioning directly targets historical interference; multi-competitor training tests whether finer discrimination reduces broad matches at the top. Neither mechanism proves product compatibility, identifies satisfied demand, or guarantees improved recommendations. Electronics’ 14.95% sampled wrong-rank rate motivates the objective comparison; pinned four-category macro validation HR@10 remains the selection criterion. Modest embedding alignment does not justify adding collapse penalties.
idea.implementation_notes:
Retain separate models and dataset routing for Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl. Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; place all checkpoints, logs and generated predictors beneath the trial directory. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, evaluation seed 42 and the SASREC_EPOCHS default of 200. Use the existing baseline optimizer, batching, architecture and learning-rate schedule unchanged initially, recording their resolved values. Do not reset the training RNG before each minibatch or validation checkpoint.

For position t, define m_t=1 when sequence[t] is nonpadding and e_t=sqrt(d)*item_emb(sequence[t]), using the same trainable item table as SASRec. Define r_t=sum_{j=0..4}(0.7^j*m_{t-j}*e_{t-j})/max(sum_{j=0..4}(0.7^j*m_{t-j}),1e-12), with out-of-range positions masked and an explicit zero vector for empty windows. Include the current input item, which precedes its next-item target. Compute the mean without embedding dropout; leave baseline dropout unchanged. This is a positional window, not elapsed-time modeling.

Use P as a bias-free d-by-d linear projection initialized to identity. Define a scalar position-dependent gate g_t=sigmoid(w^T concat(h_t,r_t)+b), initialized with w=0 and b=-1. Set a trainable scalar alpha=0 per dataset, and z_t=h_t+alpha*g_t*P(r_t). Mask padded z_t outputs to zero. Do not add an outer LayerNorm: even LN(h) changes baseline features when the correction is inactive. At initialization alpha receives gradients while the correction branch initially has zero gradients through alpha; this is expected. The SASRec input and output embedding roles remain as in the baseline, and candidate scores are dot products with its output item embeddings. Scaling r by sqrt(d) matches the baseline input convention but does not prove matching to h; log branch norms and alpha to detect domination or inactivity.

For each valid next-item target y, construct A={1,...,N}\(observed causal prefix union {y}). Include y as the positive even when it appeared previously. Draw K=32 negatives independently with replacement, uniformly from A, retaining duplicates. Use rejection sampling with an exact eligible-set fallback for small A; skip positions where A is empty and report their count. Never use later history to construct a position's feature or exclusion mask. Use mean cross-entropy over valid positions and logits [s_y,s_n1,...,s_n32], without proposal correction or an additional temperature. This is sampled-candidate discrimination. Duplicates contribute repeated denominator terms, so deduplication changes the objective. Prefix exclusion also changes which alternatives compete and may undertrain repeat-item distinctions; inspect this limitation rather than claiming catalog-wide calibration. Unobserved alternatives can still be genuine positives; defer semantic or hard-negative mining until this simpler comparison is resolved.

A separate, preregistered importance-corrected ablation could subtract log(K/M) from negative logits only, where M=|A|. The positive is deterministic and unchanged. This estimates the restricted denominator over {y} union A, with duplicates retained; its logarithm and gradients remain biased estimators. Do not apply log q(y), because the target-excluding proposal assigns it zero probability. Keep this optional ablation outside the initial four variants unless budget is explicitly allocated.

Preregister the four variants, no initial hyperparameter sweep, window 5, decay 0.7, K=32, gate bias -1 and alpha initialization 0. Use sparse checkpoint evaluations at epochs 50, 100, 150 and 200 for configurations that reach them, with the same opportunities for variants reaching the same budget rung. Evaluate the pinned protocol and select a joint four-category checkpoint/configuration by equally weighted macro HR@10, avoiding independent best-epoch selection per category. Break ties by simpler variant, then earlier checkpoint. Record every inspected checkpoint, unsuccessful trial and actual GPU-seconds, including diagnostics and failures. Profile all four datasets before committing runs; reserve 20% of the aggregate budget for contingency or a necessary final run. Give each variant complete four-category coverage at an affordable common first rung; promote only complete configurations at predetermined rungs. If initial coverage cannot fit, reduce the comparison set prospectively and document it. Four concurrent slots reduce elapsed time but do not increase the 43,200 GPU-second allowance. Each training process remains single-GPU. Preserve the nominal 200-epoch setting while recording any predetermined budget-based truncation.

Record per-category HR@10 and macro HR@10. If the host exposes per-user validation hits, retain them and use 10,000 paired bootstrap resamples with analysis seed 42, independently sampling 200 users with replacement within each category and using the same resampled users for both compared models. Report percentile 95% intervals for macro and category differences. One changed hit moves category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. These intervals condition on the training seed and fixed candidates; they do not measure training variability or correct winner-selection optimism. Use Holm adjustment if reporting hypothesis tests for prespecified comparisons. If per-user hits are unavailable, report aggregate results without inventing intervals or modifying the evaluator.

Save projection, gate, alpha, architecture settings and weights. Update the predictor writer so working/predict.py reconstructs identical fusion, padding, item mapping and category routing. In evaluation mode, verify training-side and generated-predictor scores agree on a fixed public-history minibatch. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis) using those measured values and definitions. view.model must be the actual trained module; view.log2feats must return fused features and view.predict_score must reproduce actual candidate scoring. Keep view.item_emb, user_train, meta_data and review_data compatibility accessors, without fabricating absent review data. Diagnose valid positions under eval/no_grad with a fixed probe sample; interpret sampled margins as supporting evidence. Empty category breakdowns mean attribution is unavailable, not that category errors are absent. Only histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps are available; this initial model uses histories alone. Preserve twenty real training users, five per category, for full-catalog unseen-item simulator recommendations. Treat qualitative judgments as hypothesis generation, not the selection metric. No test labels, hidden test files, external datasets or pretrained weights are used.
idea.pseudocode:
Preregister four variants and budget/checkpoint rules:
  baseline: baseline features and loss
  objective-only: baseline features, 32-negative candidate CE
  fusion-only: fused features, baseline loss
  combined: fused features, 32-negative candidate CE

For each variant and each of the four categories:
  initialize with training seed 42 using the unchanged preprocessed split
  initialize P=I, gate_w=0, gate_b=-1, alpha=0 where fusion is enabled
  for each batch (None, sequence, positive, negative):
    valid = (sequence != 0) AND (positive != 0)
    h = baseline_SASRec(sequence)
    if fusion enabled:
      e = sqrt(d) * item_emb(sequence)
      r = masked_causal_exponential_mean(e, window=5, decay=0.7)
      g = sigmoid(linear(concat(h, r)))
      z = (h + alpha * g * P(r)) * nonpadding_mask
    else:
      z = h
    if objective enabled:
      for each valid position t:
        A = catalog_without_padding - set(sequence[:t+1]) - {positive[t]}
        if A empty: skip position and increment skip counter
        negatives = uniform_draw_with_replacement(A, K=32)
        logits = score(z[t], [positive[t]] + negatives)
        position_loss = cross_entropy(logits, class_index=0)
      loss = mean(position_loss over eligible positions)
    else:
      loss = baseline_loss(z, positive, negative, valid)
    update parameters with baseline optimizer
  at a preregistered checkpoint reached by all four category runs:
    obtain pinned validation HR@10 for every category
    macro = equal_mean(four_category_HR10)
    log checkpoint opportunity, elapsed GPU-seconds and supporting diagnostics
    apply predetermined complete-configuration promotion and tie-break rules

Select the best eligible joint configuration using macro validation HR@10 only.
Serialize architecture and weights; generate working/predict.py with identical fusion.
Verify generated-predictor score parity on public histories.
Run retained diagnostic interfaces using actual fused features and actual item scores.
Report observed validation results and uncertainty only when underlying hits are available.

originality.positive: The combination is a focused, diagnosis-driven adaptation with an explicit identity-preserving initialization and a controlled objective comparison.
originality.negative: Recent-history pooling, residual gates and multi-negative objectives are established; no located source establishes novelty for this exact combination.

future_potential.positive: Controlled ablations can establish a useful basis for later timestamp conditioning, multiple interests or directional behavioral signals.
future_potential.negative: Recent histories may be noisy, sampled discrimination may not improve pinned HR@10, and the mechanism cannot resolve explicit compatibility or satisfied-demand failures.

code_difficulty.positive: The model extension is small and retains the SASRec encoder, item table and dataset routing.
code_difficulty.negative: Exact prefix-aware sampling, budgeted four-category comparisons, score parity, predictor generation and diagnostic compatibility require substantial integration care.

related_work.title: [1] gSASRec
contributions: Combines increased negative sampling with generalized BCE to address sampling-induced overconfidence.
limitations: Increasing negatives alone does not reproduce its calibration correction.
The supplied evidence does not establish results under this exact RecHarness protocol.

related_work.title: [2] Scalable Cross-Entropy
contributions: Approximates catalog-wide cross-entropy using selective computation focused on informative competitors.
limitations: The proposed uniform candidate cross-entropy is a simpler objective and does not reproduce this method or exact catalog-wide cross-entropy.

related_work.title: [3] Hierarchical Long and Short-Term User Preference Modeling
contributions: Models multiple persistent preferences and matches them against recent behavior with temporal fusion.
limitations: The proposed recent-history residual omits richer routing and temporal mechanisms.
Recent preference matching cannot establish functional compatibility or whether ownership has satisfied a need.

related_work.title: [4] Official SASRec implementation
contributions: Provides implementation conventions including zero padding and square-root embedding scaling.
limitations: It does not specify or validate the proposed five-item exponential-mean fusion.
The pinned RecHarness baseline remains the implementation authority for this experiment.

related_work.title: [5] ReZero Is All You Need: Fast Convergence at Large Depth
contributions: Uses zero-initialized trainable residual scaling to preserve an identity mapping at initialization.
limitations: It does not establish recommendation gains or validate the proposed recent-history branch.

related_work.title: [6] On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled recommendation metrics can disagree with full-catalog evaluation and alter model comparisons.
limitations: It motivates restricting claims to the pinned evaluator, rather than changing the authorized evaluation protocol.

related_work.title: [7] On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains how optimizing noisy selection criteria can overfit model selection and bias reported performance.
limitations: Sparse checkpoint schedules and preregistration reduce opportunities for selection bias but do not eliminate it.

related_work.title: Highway Networks
contributions: Motivates negatively biased sigmoid gates for initially suppressing transformed branches.
limitations: A negative gate bias alone does not make a residual branch exactly inactive; zero residual scaling provides that property here.

related_work.title: TensorFlow Candidate Sampling Reference
contributions: Describes candidate-sampling objectives and expected-count corrections.
limitations: Corrections must match the actual proposal and deterministic positive inclusion.
Proposal correction cannot recover catalog alternatives excluded from sampling support.

related_work.title: Recommendation evaluation inference at scale
contributions: Provides support for bootstrap and randomization approaches to uncertainty in recommendation evaluation.
limitations: User resampling under fixed models and candidates does not measure training variability or remove adaptive selection bias.

related_work.title: Hyperband: A Novel Bandit-Based Approach to Hyperparameter Optimization
contributions: Supports allocating resources through successive evaluation and promotion of configurations.
limitations: Early performance may misrank slow-learning configurations.
The proposed measured-time, four-category allocation is an adaptation rather than a reproduction of Hyperband.
